records.label: Publish content and join a BitTorrent swarm

fields.label: Name
fields.value: Publish content and join a BitTorrent swarm

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: A publisher creates torrent metadata, publishes a .torrent file or magnet link, seeds the complete content, and clients discover peers and exchange verified pieces.

value.action: Prepare the files and choose piece length and metadata parameters.
Generate torrent metadata and piece hashes; v1 uses SHA-1 and v2 uses SHA-256/Merkle-tree structures.
Publish the .torrent file or magnet link through an index or another distribution channel.
Make a complete copy available so initial downloaders can obtain pieces.
Discover peers through trackers, DHT, and/or peer exchange.
Exchange pieces with peers; verify received pieces against metadata hashes.
Reassemble verified pieces into the file and optionally continue seeding.

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: A client selects available pieces, prioritizes rare pieces to preserve diversity, and uses choking/unchoking policies plus optimistic unchoking to manage upload partners.

value.action: Track missing pieces and the pieces advertised by connected peers.
Prefer rare pieces to reduce the chance that a piece disappears from the swarm.
Use choking/unchoking decisions to allocate upload bandwidth.
Use optimistic unchoking to try a peer that may become a better exchange partner and help newcomers acquire initial pieces.
Verify and share successfully received pieces, increasing swarm capacity.

records.label: BitTorrent v2 integrity verification and hybrid compatibility

fields.label: Name
fields.value: BitTorrent v2 integrity verification and hybrid compatibility

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: BitTorrent v2 uses SHA-256 and Merkle-tree-based hashes for finer-grained integrity checks. Hybrid metadata includes v1 and v2 hashes to support older and newer clients.

value.action: Hash content at file and piece granularity using the v2 format.
Obtain the torrent metadata or equivalent magnet metadata.
Transfer pieces from one or more peers or web seeds.
Verify the received content against the expected hash tree.
For hybrid torrents, use the included v1/v2 metadata to interoperate with compatible legacy and v2 clients.

fields.label: Name
fields.value: Peer discovery with tracker, DHT, and PEX

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: Peer discovery can combine centralized trackers, decentralized DHT lookup, and peer exchange. These mechanisms are complementary rather than mutually exclusive.

value.action: Read tracker endpoints from torrent metadata when present.
Ask tracker services for peers, if reachable.
Join the DHT via a bootstrap server and look up peers when DHT is enabled.
Exchange peer information with connected peers using PEX when supported.
Connect to candidate peers and repeat discovery as peer membership changes.

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: The base protocol exposes peer IP addresses and does not provide anonymity. VPNs, seedboxes, Tor-like systems, or I2P change the trust and visibility model but introduce their own constraints.

value.action: Connect to swarm peers; peer endpoints may be visible to other participants.
If using a VPN or seedbox, recognize that the intermediary can observe some user activity or network metadata.
If using Tor-like routing, consider client compatibility and network impact; the article cautions that most clients are not designed for safe torrenting over Tor.
Treat downloaded payloads as untrusted and verify integrity; a valid hash proves correspondence to metadata, not that the content is benign or legally authorized.

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: A swarm can lose availability when all complete seeds disappear. Multiple discovery paths do not solve missing-content availability; durable seeds, bundling, or cross-torrent strategies can help.

value.action: Download pieces and optionally seed them after completion.
Remain online to provide a complete source for missing pieces.
If no complete seed remains and required pieces are missing, the download may stall indefinitely.
Improve long-term availability by maintaining seeds, bundling related content, or using proposed cross-torrent cooperation.
